calls.head: Don’t buy Wolf’s slump against the Kraken
calls.body: Wolf has been shaky against the Kraken since 2023-24, well below his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if he looks like himself tonight.

calls.body: The Flames shoot from anywhere, and the Kraken are one of the league’s worst at stopping it. The Kraken’s goalie had better be ready from the opening faceoff.

surprises.head: Dustin Wolf got lit up
surprises.body: Wolf allowed 6 goals on 27 shots, worth 2.9 expected goals: 3.1 more than expected. Starting goalies have a night this rough about once every 40 starts.

story.head: The Kraken pile it on the Flames
paras: The Flames’ Joel Farabee played his 500th NHL game. Berkly Catton struck first for the Kraken early in the first. Mackie Samoskevich scored his first goal for Seattle 2:18 later to make it 2-0. Bobby McMann made it 3-0, 3:00 later. Shane Wright made it 4-0 midway through the second. Samoskevich scored again late in the second to make it 5-0. Morgan Frost got the Flames on the board on the power play late in the third. Jordan Eberle made it 6-1 for the Kraken with 4:56 left.

Don’t let the score fool you: the chances were a lot closer than that. Joey Daccord made 32 saves for the Kraken, and Dustin Wolf allowed six goals on 27 shots. By our Swing measure, Brandon Montour had the best night of anyone. The Kraken improved to 2-1-0, and the Flames fell to 0-3-0.
